requirements.text: The web app is released from one commit of main through release/pages and deployed with wrangler after the acceptance walk passes, staging first.
One address serves the app, crankmagic.com, and the only public contact is admin@crankmagic.com.
A signed-in person's library saves itself to the cloud and follows them to any device; a conflict is put to the person and the other version is held 30 days.
Every /api/* request passes Cloudflare Access and is verified again by the Worker: signature, audience, issuer, expiry and a named person.
The web app follows the r3 design system: its tokens, Satoshi type and the brass accent, in dark and light.
A landing page at / for a signed-out visitor with no library in the browser; anyone else goes straight to Decks.
A Settings page: Account, Appearance, Prices (USD and EUR), Data, and About with every data set's date and the version.
Delete account: a Worker route removes the person's snapshots, head and user row; removing them from Access stays Rob's runbook step.
For a signed-in person, 'Tell me when it's ready' on Play is a switch stored with the account; no mailing list.
Import from an Archidekt link through a Worker route, with a size limit and nothing stored.
Start from a precon, from a list refreshed with the card data from MTGJSON.
Outside data is read live first, then from the reader's cache (IndexedDB: 7 days for records, 24 hours for prices), then from a refreshed store.
Card images always come from Scryfall's CDN, through the browser's and the worker's caches, and are never stored by us.
Stores only where live cannot do the job: the name index, the engine's oracle snapshot, one dated price snapshot, EDHREC ranks and co-play, precons, and our derived graph and strategies.
A scheduled GitHub Actions run of tools/refresh.mjs publishes dated keys and current.json to R2 and keeps 7 runs; a run that fails its proof publishes nothing.
The Worker serves /data/* from R2, and the app reads current.json in place of ?v= pins.
Settings › About shows every data set's date, and anything past its lifetime is labeled stale.
A game pins the oracle snapshot and card-definition version it started with, so a replay is identical.
A rules adjudication log citing the CR, the card's rulings, the release notes and the Commander page, and a scheduled Comprehensive Rules check.
Honor each source's terms: Scryfall's User-Agent, rate and bulk files; EDHREC read gently on a schedule; Wizards' texts cited and not redistributed.
The browser reaches only api.scryfall.com and loads images only from Scryfall's CDNs; every other source goes through the Worker or the scheduled job.
Offline still works: the worker keeps the last good copy of every stored set and the reader's cache keeps what they opened.
Rate limits on /api/*, per identity and per IP.
Workers observability logs, alerts on 5xx and on sync conflicts, and a weekly check.
D1 Time Travel's window confirmed, and a nightly export of D1 to R2.
Accounts are invite-only through the Access 'Invited' policy; the free plan caps it at 50 people.
CME plays Rob's seven decks deterministically with hidden information held, writing its journal and checkpoints through a storage adapter.
The house pilot, the engine's own opponent, sees only its seat and costs nothing per game.
Deck legality is checked at prepare against a dated banned list, refusing by name.
One Durable Object per match runs CME, holds the authoritative state and hides hands.
A WebSocket on the Durable Object carries ordered view updates and receipts, with no polling.
The Worker creates, joins and leaves tables and hands a seat to an Access identity; identity stays out of the engine.
The lobby per r3's 2b design: invites by e-mail, link and QR, table rules, and auto-launch that waits for every human seat.
Reconnect sends a fresh permitted view; a game never concedes silently and AI takes over only by agreement.
A finished game files its record under the deck and syncs with the account; a guest's deck never overwrites the host's library.
Card definitions are served to the room from R2, not bundled.
Hidden information holds in network payloads, logs and reconnect snapshots.
The AI door: its own Access application (Google with MFA, never the emailed code), an AI allowlist in D1, the key as a Worker secret, spend caps, and a log of every call.
The privacy page says what goes to the AI before any AI feature is switched on.
Every card is compiled and reconciled into card definitions shipped as data; a card that cannot be is refused, naming what it lacks.
A playtest table on staging for Grok Bot's four agents, whose games export seed, journal and per-seat projections.
CME is the only engine: Forge, the local Windows host and the tunnel are retired.
The Coach's logic through the AI door, the Lab's data-driven strategy, and the accounts' later features if Rob still wants them.
An architecture page draws the final state from engram's graph, with a current-state toggle.
github.io is retired from main; nothing names it.
